facts.fact: The World Bank's appraisal-stage PID states that the EHR (Dossier Médical Informatisé, DMI) is fully installed and used in 50 per cent of university hospitals and installed but partially used in the other 50 per cent; in regional hospitals 32 per cent are fully operational, 52 per cent installed but partially used and 16 per cent have none; no counts of hospitals are given and the figures are undated, so the PID's date of 2 April 2025 is used.

The World Bank PID states that in district hospitals and primary health centres (CSBs) EHR systems are neither installed nor used, against a stated base of over 2,000 CSBs; the statement is undated, so the PID's date of 2 April 2025 is used.

The World Bank PID, describing primary health care, states that the health system remains largely paper-based, that the Electronic Health Records pilot (DMI) faces connectivity and functionality issues, and that there is no unified registry for chronic conditions; undated, so the PID's date of 2 April 2025 is used.
